marquee:
Use case: ads-marketing.
Create ONE final, exceptionally well art-directed Chrome Web Store advertising banner for "LinkedIn MCP Bridge". Wide 5:2 format, target 1400x560. This is capability-led product marketing, NOT a software screenshot.
The actual product lets a user's AI assistant search people on LinkedIn, read and reply to conversations, and draft and schedule posts. Communicate these concrete benefits immediately.
Design direction: confident Swiss editorial typography, crisp flat ink, warm ivory background #f6f3eb, near-black navy #14283b, brilliant cobalt #1955e6. Tight typographic hierarchy with generous intentional margins. Absolutely no 3D, no glass, glow, gradients, sparkles, robot heads, cables, abstract connectivity logos, generic stock visuals, or photorealism.
Layout: left 52% contains small product name at top, enormous bold tasteful grotesk sans-serif headline in three short lines, and one short supporting line below. Right 42% contains three beautifully arranged oversized flat editorial strips, slightly offset, like printed task notes. These notes are marketing examples, not app UI; no window chrome, buttons, rounded dashboard cards, fake screens or tiny text. Each strip has a large simple black hand-drawn editorial symbol at left and a highly legible concrete task at right: magnifying glass with person, two speech bubbles, calendar with pen. Use one cobalt strip with white text and two ivory strips with black text and thin ink rules. A restrained orange underline adds one small contrast accent. The result must feel like a real paid campaign from a serious creative studio, not a SaaS template.
Exact text, and ONLY this text:
Small brand at top left: "LinkedIn MCP Bridge"
Huge headline: "Less busywork.\nMore meaningful\nconnections."
Supporting line: "Put your AI assistant to work on LinkedIn."
Three task notes on right:
"Find the right people"
"Read and reply to messages"
"Draft and schedule posts"
The text must be flawlessly spelled, clearly legible, not cramped. Headline is strongest element. All objects contained with safe margins. No logos of LinkedIn or other companies. No disclaimers, technical setup, platform requirements, beta badges or subtitles. Single finished full-bleed banner.
